description: Kindle Paperwhite 3 (Wario, machine 4091) on stock firmware 5.16.2.1.1: the stock kernel the handoff module loads into, and the physical plan of the jump
supported_zh: Kindle Paperwhite 3（第 7 代，2015 年款，机身背面型号 DP75SDI），固件 5.16.2.1.1
supported_en: Kindle Paperwhite (7th generation, 2015; model DP75SDI on the back), firmware 5.16.2.1.1
supported_why: what the E101 screen tells someone whose Kindle this build refuses (installer/screens/render_screens.py). Amazon's own name for the model, not this project's "PW3": the person reading it knows what they bought, not what the board is called. The generation and the year are both there because the model number on the back is shared with the 2013 Paperwhite, and the firmware because the handover runs that kernel's own code (stock_kernel_why)
identity_limit_why: the upper bound of the one-to-one region of the page table the handoff runs under, which the module builds in the half this kernel leaves to user space. It equals this kernel's TASK_SIZE, but that is a coincidence of 3G/1G: PAGE_OFFSET (0xc0000000) and PHYS_OFFSET (0x80000000) differ here, so the kernel's lowmem mapping is not one to one and a window has to be made. On a 2G/2G Kindle the two are equal and lowmem itself is the window (docs/design/porting-to-other-models.md section 6)
cmdline_base: log_pos_goal=0x8fff0000 console=ttymxc0,115200 ro ip=off quiet video=mxcepdcfb:E60,bpp=8,x_mem=3M
cmdline_base_why: the stock command line without root= and rootwait (devicedata.c checks the running system's against it); the console, the EPDC's video mode and the log position stay as stock has them
stock_kernel_why: the stock kernel this firmware ships, as /proc/version and uname report it. The handover runs that kernel's own pm_test_show and L2 cache functions and checks their bodies against stock_functions, so another build of it cannot be used; devicedata.c refuses it as another firmware and the screen says so (E101) rather than leaving someone to restart and tap again for ever
device_data_profile_why: the struct in boot/devicedata/devicedata.c that carries the same facts as this file for the compiled helper, which is what the device is actually checked against. boot/build_launcher.py passes it as -DDD_PROFILE, and tools/tests/test_profile_matches_devicedata.py refuses a build whose two halves disagree -- the JSON is what the boot module and the E101 screen are made from, the struct is what the check on the device reads, and one without the other is a device that refuses to start for no stated reason
forbidden_why: payload destinations stay in the low 128 MiB, below anything the stock system may still have in use above it
stock_cpuid_why: the CPU identity register (MIDR) the handoff's hardware gate reads (boot/handoff/native-handoff.h): real Wario silicon, as the stock kernel's own MIDR check reports it. The QEMU emulator reports 0x410fc090 instead, and only an emulator build may substitute that (boot/build_module.py --emulator); a release build's gate must be the device's number or it is not the device it says
stock_files_why: the four stock files the entry proves are the firmware's own before it runs anything from them or draws a screen through one (boot/devicedata/devicedata.c identity table): /sbin/init and /etc/upstart/init.sh are the same 1,360-byte script here, /sbin/init.exe the Lab126 launcher, and /usr/sbin/eips every screen. The helper reads these numbers from the compiled struct, this file is what the build and this test read, and tools/tests/test_profile_matches_devicedata.py refuses a build whose two copies disagree
stock_functions_source: function bodies of the stock 5.16.2.1.1 kernel (image sha256 3915c4c0d09566d674a8d2b4ca249292a056e882d5291fe3997f1dc6ca49e02d), read from a device's own eMMC; only their sizes and hashes are kept
